scenes.event: Elizabeth and her colleagues discuss personal changes over coffee.
scenes.description: Elizabeth sits by the window in the company coffee corner, drinking coffee and staring blankly at her notebook. Her colleague Ella notices her expression and asks with concern if something is wrong. Another colleague, David, overhears and joins the conversation.

characters.name: Ella Thompson
characters.description: A supportive and empathetic colleague who is in her late 20s; Female; Age: 28; Occupation: Project Coordinator; Personality: compassionate, observant, thoughtful; Values: teamwork, personal growth, work-life balance; Interests: journaling, mindfulness practices, indie music; Experiences: recently transitioned to a more flexible work schedule to focus on mental health, mentored a new employee through a difficult project, worked remotely during a family crisis.

characters.name: David Carter
characters.description: A 30-year-old office worker who is curious and observant; Male; Age: 30; Occupation: Marketing Analyst; Personality: Analytical, empathetic, adaptable; Values: Personal growth, intellectual curiosity, work-life balance; Interests: Philosophy, photography, journaling; Experiences: Successfully led a team through a major company rebrand, recently started attending weekly meditation sessions, has a habit of offering thoughtful advice to friends and coworkers.

actions.action: notices Elizabeth's expression and approaches her
actions.dialogue: Hey Elizabeth, you look like you're a million miles away. Everything okay?
I guess... I was just thinking about whether I've changed, or if I'm just pretending to be someone I'm not.

actions.action: comforts Elizabeth with a personal example
actions.dialogue: I used to hate coffee, but now I can't live without it. You know, people change, and that's okay. It's part of growing.
That's true, Ella. I think we all go through phases where we question who we are or what we like. It's a sign you're evolving, Elizabeth.

scenes.plot: Elizabeth is struggling with her sense of self and whether her recent changes are authentic. Her colleagues, Ella and David, provide support and perspective, helping her to see that personal growth and change are natural parts of life.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore Elizabeth's internal conflict and reveal her values of self-consistency and personal growth through a meaningful conversation with supportive coworkers.

chunk.text: Elizabeth sits by the window in the company coffee corner, drinking coffee and staring blankly at her notebook. Her colleague Ella notices her expression and asks with concern if something is wrong. Elizabeth admits she is thinking about whether she has changed, and Ella comforts her with the example of her own transition from hating coffee to being unable to live without it. Elizabeth falls silent, displaying ambivalence regarding self-consistency and change. This conversation reveals Elizabeth's inner struggle and hints that she may be going through a critical phase of re-knowing herself.
